'1.1. To provide guidelines on how to assess and manage newborn with neonatal hypoglycemia to
prevent brain damage.
2. DEFINITION&ABBREVIATION
2.1. Hypoglycemia - a serum glucose value of <45 mg/dl in a term or preterm neonate which
suggest clinically significant hypoglycemia are non-specific and include jitteriness, irritability,
high pitched cry, cyanosis, apnea, seizures, lethargy, hypotonia or poor feeding.
2.2. Neonatal Hypoglycemia - newborn's blood glucose level is too low to support normal brain
function.
2.3. BSL - Blood Sugar Level, measured by a blood glucose monitor (glucometer) and reagent strip
in birth center and postnatalwards.
2.4. lBC - True Blood Clucose, as measured on a blood gas analyzer in NICU or by laboratory
measurement.
2.5. EMR - Electronic Medical Records
2.6. MCC - Medica Cloud Care system / HIS (Hospital lnformation System)
2.7. NICU - Neonatal lntensive Care Unit

3.3. Nurses (Head Nurse, Charge Nurse and Staff Nurse)

3.3.2. Assess, reassess and monitor patient with hypoglycemia.

5. PROCEDURE
5.1. The physician and nurse on duty will assess the patient with potential risk and predisposing
factors to develop hypoglycemia which follows:
5.1.1. lmpendlng birth of an infant of a motherwith diabetes.
5.2. Management of infants with risk factors for or diagnosis of hypoglycemia in OBSN:
9.2.1. Measure BSL or TBC on blood gas analyzer.
5.2.1.1. Within one hour of arrival in nursery (or as ordered by pediatric specialist).
5.2.1.2. lf TBC > 2.6 mmol/l- repeat before next feed, or 3 hourly if infant nil orally.
5.2.1.3. lf TBC < 2.6 mmol/l, repeat TBC in t hour
5.2.1.4. Measure TBC before feeds if feed due
5.2.1.5. Clucose monitoring may be discontinued when 3 consecutive TBC readings
>2.6mmol/L.
5.3. Physician willenter orders in the doctors order sheet in MCC.
5.4. Nurse on duty will veri! physician's order and implement treatment as prescribed.
5.5. Re-assessment of patients receiving treatment for hypoglycemia shall be performed.
5.6. Document allthe procedures done in the patient's electronic medical records (EMR).
